description: The Internet Infrastructure Map tracks the historical evolution of the undersea cable network, global internet peering capacity and IP allocation over time on an interactive map with a year control. The page states that underlying data can be downloaded as JSON files: all_cables.json, a GeoJSON collection of all submarine cables with properties such as name, ready-for-service year, decommission year, owners and landing points; year-summaries.json with short descriptions of notable years; and meta.json with the covered year range. Producer: an independent project (map.kmcd.dev) using TeleGeography for modern cables, PeeringDB for exchange points and peering facilities, and submarinenetworks.com and archived maps for historical cables. Coverage: global. Access: view on the map page; the JSON files are offered under 'Raw Data & Formats'. Licence and cost: free to view; no licence was stated, and the source data carry their providers' own terms. Caveats: no licence for the compiled files, and the historical cable data are curated from mixed sources. Simulation uses: the cable and landing-point geometry can seed network-flow and resilience models of international connectivity. Related record: the CAIDA PeeringDB archive (data-caida-peeringdb-historical-archive).
